title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint: Low back pain

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on RA, Temp 98.6 F, RR 16

Recent Labs: Hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, White Blood Cell Count 7.0 x 10^9/L, Platelets 210 x 10^9/L.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, weight change.
Respiratory: Denies shortness of breath, cough.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for low back pain; denies joint swelling.
Neurological: Denies numbness or tingling in lower extremities.
All other systems: Reviewed and negative.

Social History: Retired; lives with husband. Non-smoker. Occasional gardening.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had osteoarthritis.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is a 69-year-old female presenting for evaluation of low back pain. She reports a dull ache in the lumbar region that began approximately two weeks ago. She notes the pain is exacerbated by prolonged standing and improved with rest. She denies any radiating pain to the legs, incontinence, or recent falls. She has tried over-the-counter heat packs with moderate relief.

[Today's Update] The patient states the low back pain has persisted for several days but has not worsened in intensity. She continues to use heat and reports some improvement during periods of rest. She denies any new symptoms.

Medication List:
Tiotropium (Spiriva) 18mcg inhaler
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Naproxen 500mg as needed for back pain

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
Musculoskeletal: Tenderness noted over the lumbar spine. Range of motion is limited by discomfort. No spinal step-off noted. Strength is 5/5 in bilateral lower extremities. Sensation is intact to light touch.

Problem List:
- COPD
- Status post appendectomy
- Status post cholecystectomy
- Status post tonsillectomy
- Low back pain

Assessment:
1. Low back pain: The patient's symptoms appear to be musculoskeletal in nature. She is stable regarding her primary chronic condition.
2. COPD: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is stable.

Plan:
1. Low back pain: Will monitor symptoms and continue conservative management with heat and scheduled Naproxen as needed.
2. COPD: Continue current tiotropium regimen. 

Electronically signed,
A. Rivera, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: The provider addressed COPD at this visit (status and plan documented), so it is supported and coded.

distractors.why: Status plus a plan in the assessment supports the diagnosis.

hccs.label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease/Interstitial Lung Disorders/and Other Chronic Lung Disorders
